Thresholds of the data-entry checks

Source: R/check_detset.R
check_settings.Rd

Returns the thresholds check_detset() uses, with any given here in place of the defaults. Each default is a stated choice that the data do not fix; change it when the study needs another.

Usage

check_settings(...)

Arguments

...

Named thresholds to change.

Value

A named list of every threshold.

Details

  • extent: the study extent as c(lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max). Without it, a deployment is outside the extent when it lies further from the median deployment position than both outlier_km and outlier_mult times the median distance of the deployments from that position.

  • outlier_km (20) and outlier_mult (10): see extent.

  • station_tol_m (100): one station's coordinate sets further apart than this are two coordinate sets.

  • reuse_m (1000): one station's coordinate sets further apart than this are a station name reused at another place.

  • same_place_m (10): two station names closer than this share one place.

  • year_off_days (300): a deployment that starts this long before its first detection, or ends this long after its last, is a year off.

  • download_tol_s (3600): a recovery more than this after the download.

  • depth_tol_m (1): a receiver deeper than the bathymetry by more than this.

  • codetect_s (5): two receivers that log one transmitter within this many seconds heard one transmission.

  • move_min (20) and move_tv (0.75): a deployment's co-detection partners change when, at some date with at least move_min co-detections on each side, the total variation distance between the partner shares before and after reaches move_tv. On a 600 m grid a move of one spacing scored 0.40 to 0.61, below the threshold.

  • tz_window_h (15): detections this close outside a deployment boundary count towards a time-zone offset. An offset is confirmed only where the deployments detecting near the other end leave it empty, so a receiver that logs on deck after recovery is not read as one.

  • dst_min (30) and dst_max (90): a step back in time of this many minutes, in the order the rows arrived, marks a daylight-saving jump. Rows must be in the order each receiver logged them; see check_detset() for what the check cannot see.

  • p_min (0.001): a receiver hears a position when the detection field gives it at least this probability there.

  • max_liberty_years (no default): detections more than this many years after release are flagged by long_after_release, which runs without a tag life, as for a GLATOS export. Give the longest life of the study's tag models, from the manufacturer's specifications.

  • reappear_gap_days (365): a transmitter silent for longer than this, then heard only at stations it never used before, is flagged by reappeared_elsewhere: a code reused by another project, or a tag moved by a person.

  • duplicate_tol_s (0): two detections of one transmitter on one receiver this many seconds apart or less are one detection, as in filter_duplicates(); 0 matches exact stamps only.

Examples

check_settings(station_tol_m = 50)$station_tol_m
#> [1] 50
